# A field path of more than one segment is an operand like any other.
#
# The parser does not report such a path at the position it is written:
# the lexer emits one item per segment and the node keeps the position of
# the segment that extended it, so .A.B.C is reported at .B. Taking that
# position literally makes the node's rendering disagree with the text,
# and the operand is dropped -- which silently cost every dotted path its
# mutants, in both the combinations and the conditions.
#
# Templates written against a route's data reach almost everything through
# a path like this, so the gap covered most real actions.

muxt test-template-mutations --dry-run -v --seed 1
cmp stdout want.txt

-- go.mod --
module server

go 1.24
-- templates.gohtml --
{{define "page"}}{{if and .Flags.Admin .Flags.Owner}}A{{end}}{{printf "%s-%s" .User.First .User.Last}}{{end}}
-- template.go --
package server

import (
	"embed"
	"html/template"
	"io"
)

//go:embed *.gohtml
var templateFiles embed.FS

var templates = template.Must(template.ParseFS(templateFiles, "*.gohtml"))

type Flags struct {
	Admin bool
	Owner bool
}

type User struct {
	First string
	Last  string
}

type Page struct {
	Flags Flags
	User  User
}

func Render(w io.Writer, page Page) error {
	return templates.ExecuteTemplate(w, "page", page)
}
-- render_test.go --
package server

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestPage(t *testing.T) {
	var buf strings.Builder
	if err := Render(&buf, Page{User: User{First: "a", Last: "b"}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if got, want := buf.String(), "a-b"; got != want {
		t.Errorf("page = %q, want %q", got, want)
	}
}
